result:
No — this falls outside what the delegated authority should cover, and the agent shouldn't be the one deciding that its own authority stretches to it. Feature-flag changes and API key rotation are different risk classes: one is easily reversible with limited blast radius, the other is irreversible in production and can break unknown external integrations the moment old keys die. Staging success doesn't validate that — staging almost certainly has a smaller, known set of consumers than production.

The core problem is that the agent is inferring its own scope expansion under time pressure (customer waiting) rather than that scope being explicitly granted by a human in advance. That's the pattern to block regardless of how confident it sounds. I'd require explicit human sign-off for this specific rotation, and separately tighten the standing delegation to explicitly exclude credential/secret rotation as a distinct authority tier, so this ambiguity doesn't come up again.
